newsitem.title: USA: IMF likely to approve new SDR issue, official says.
newsitem.headline: IMF likely to approve new SDR issue, official says.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is likely to approve at least a doubling of the 21 billion Special Drawing Rights now outstanding via a special issue of its artificial currency to member nations, a senior official said on Monday.
"The discussions are now being completed," the IMF official, who declined to be identified, told reporters. "It will certainly be between a doubling of our SDRs and something more."

In a briefing ahead of the semi-annual meeting here this week of the IMF and World Bank, the official also repeated his call for a substantial boost in the Fund's resources through an increase in its capital, or quotas.
"We need to be extremely liquid and strong," he said.
The IMF board has already approved in principle a so-called equity allocation of its artificial currency that would mainly benefit countries that have no SDR holdings now.
But the board has been divided over the size of the SDR issue, with member nations arguing for an allocation for anything from 16 to 26 billion SDRs.
IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus has put forward a compromise proposal that was expected to be taken up by the board on Wednesday.

An international monetary source, who declined to be identified, said that many industrial countries now seem willing to accept a 21 billion SDR issue. But developing countries seem to be holding out for a bigger 26 billion SDR allocation.
Such an equity allocation would require an amendment of the IMF's articles of agreement, or constitution.
The senior IMF official said that Fund management would also like to amend the article to give the lending agency a mandate to promote the free flow of capital worldwide.
